implementation.operator: begin_call spawns a live adapter worker and fsyncs the ledger; inject_network_fault drops the owner; recover() reclaims by thread id when the worker is alive, else writes an ABANDONED receipt; missing ledger returns UNKNOWN never SUCCESS. Independent readers json.loads the ledger and live-threads files and check /proc.

negative_controls.description: Uncancelled complete is a normal SUCCESS receipt with no ABANDONED record. The same call cancelled by a network fault leaves an unowned RUNNING adapter thread until recover().
Deleting the ledger entry makes recover() report UNKNOWN, not SUCCESS. A mutant that keys only on live threads reports SUCCESS and fails this test.

question: When a cross-vendor adapter call (Codex MCP thread) is cancelled mid-request by a network fault, does crash recovery either reclaim the thread by id or record an explicit ABANDONED receipt? PASS requires: no thread id is left in a running state with no owner, and the receipt names which of the two outcomes occurred.
